topic: War of Jenkins' Ear: Britain vs Spain
title: The War Britain Fought Over One Man's Pickled Ear
description: In 1739, Britain declared war on Spain over a sailor's severed ear, pickled in a jar. But the scene everyone pictures from Parliament almost certainly never happened, and the real reason for the war runs deeper than one ear. AI-narrated history commentary.

hook_candidates.text: An ear in a jar that started a war between Britain and Spain in 1739.
Would an empire really declare war over a pickled ear? Britain did, in 1739.
The most famous scene from the 'Ear War' almost certainly never happened.
In 1731, Spanish sailors sliced off a British captain's ear. It started a war eight years later.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks modern wars have serious causes, because they want to prove an empire once fought over a single pickled ear.
contradicted_belief: Most people believe a war between Britain and Spain could never start over one man's ear.
closing_comment: The real twist about the Jenkins' Ear war is that Britain wanted a war with Spain for trade routes years before Jenkins lost his ear.

sources.note: Confirms modern research found Jenkins never personally appeared before Parliament with the ear
Confirms the 1731 ear-cutting incident and Britain's June 1739 declaration of war on Spain
